title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 7.

questions.question: What does Paul state is good for a man regarding women?
options: It is good for a man not to touch a woman
It is good for a man to marry a woman
It is good for a man to have many wives
It is good for a man to be single
questions.correctAnswer: It is good for a man not to touch a woman
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 7:1 that it is good for a man not to touch a woman.

questions.question: What does Paul advise to avoid fornication?
options: Let every man have his own wife
Let every man live in celibacy
Let every man take multiple wives
questions.correctAnswer: Let every man have his own wife
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 7:2, Paul advises that to avoid fornication, every man should have his own wife.

questions.question: According to Paul, who has power over the body in a marriage?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:4 states that the wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband; and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.

questions.question: True or False: Paul commands that the husband should not put away his wife.
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 7:11, Paul commands that if a wife departs, she should remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband, and that the husband should not put away his wife.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the unmarried and widows?
options: It is good for them to abide as they are
They should seek a new partner
questions.correctAnswer: It is good for them to abide as they are
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 7:8, Paul states that it is good for the unmarried and widows to abide even as he is.

questions.question: True or False: Paul believes it is better to burn than to marry.
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 7:9, Paul states that if they cannot contain, it is better to marry than to burn.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 7, what instruction comes first regarding marriage?
options: Let not the wife depart from her husband
Let every man have his own wife
Defraud ye not one the other
questions.correctAnswer: Let every man have his own wife
questions.explanation: The first instruction regarding marriage in 1 Corinthians 7 is found in verse 2: 'Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife.'

questions.question: What should a husband and wife not do to each other?
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 7:5, Paul instructs not to defraud one another, except with consent for a time.

questions.question: True or False: Paul claims that the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:14 states that the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and vice versa.

questions.question: What does Paul say about circumcision in 1 Corinthians 7?
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 7:19, Paul states that circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping the commandments of God is what matters.

questions.question: What should every man do according to his calling?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:24 instructs every man to abide in the same calling wherein he was called.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:2 advise to avoid fornication?
options: Let every man have his own wife
Let every woman have her own husband
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:2 advises that to avoid fornication, each man should have his own wife and each woman should have her own husband, emphasizing the importance of marital relationships to maintain sexual purity.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 7:5, why should couples come together again after a period of fasting and prayer?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:5 states that couples should come together again after fasting and prayer to prevent Satan from tempting them due to lack of self-control.

questions.question: What is said about a wife and her husband in 1 Corinthians 7:4?
options: Neither has power over their own body
Both are free to do as they wish
questions.correctAnswer: Neither has power over their own body
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:4 indicates that the wife does not have power over her own body, nor does the husband have power over his own body, highlighting the mutual responsibility in marriage.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:9 suggest for those who cannot contain themselves?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:9 states that if individuals cannot contain themselves, it is better for them to marry than to burn with passion, emphasizing the legitimacy of marriage.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 7:15, what is stated about a brother or sister if an unbelieving spouse departs?
options: They are bound to the marriage
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:15 clarifies that if an unbelieving spouse departs, the believer is not under bondage and is called to peace, which implies freedom to remarry.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 7:20, what should every man do?
options: Abide in the same calling he was called
questions.correctAnswer: Abide in the same calling he was called
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:20 instructs that every man should remain in the same calling in which he was called, emphasizing contentment in one's current state.

questions.question: What is indicated about circumcision in 1 Corinthians 7:19?
options: It is nothing compared to keeping God's commandments
It is required for all believers
questions.correctAnswer: It is nothing compared to keeping God's commandments
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:19 states that circumcision and uncircumcision are of no significance; rather, what matters is keeping the commandments of God.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 7:33 describe the concern of a married man?
options: He cares for the things of the world
questions.correctAnswer: He cares for the things of the world
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:33 notes that a married man cares for the things that are of the world, particularly how he may please his wife, indicating a balance between worldly and spiritual responsibilities.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:28 say about marrying?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:28 states that if someone marries, they have not sinned, affirming the validity of marriage even while acknowledging potential worldly troubles.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 7:10, the wife is commanded to depart from her husband.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:10 commands that the wife should not depart from her husband, affirming the sanctity of the marriage bond.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 7:22 states that a servant called in the Lord is considered the Lord's freeman.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:22 confirms that a servant who is called in the Lord is the Lord's freeman, highlighting the spiritual freedom that comes from faith in Christ.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Corinthians 7:40, Paul expresses that a widow is happier if she remarries.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:40 suggests that Paul believes a widow is happier if she remains as she is, indicating his preference for remaining single.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 7.

questions.question: What does Paul suggest about the state of those who have wives in 1 Corinthians 7:29?
options: They should act as though they had none
They should separate from their wives
questions.correctAnswer: They should act as though they had none
questions.explanation: Paul states that those who have wives should act as though they had none because the time is short, indicating a focus on spiritual matters over earthly attachments (1 Corinthians 7:29).

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 7:31, how should believers use the world?
questions.explanation: Paul instructs believers to use the world as not abusing it, recognizing that the fashion of this world is temporary (1 Corinthians 7:31).

questions.question: What is said about the difference between a wife and a virgin in 1 Corinthians 7:34?
options: A wife pleases her husband; a virgin pleases the Lord
A virgin is bound by the law
A wife is more holy than a virgin
questions.correctAnswer: A wife pleases her husband; a virgin pleases the Lord
questions.explanation: Paul explains that the unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord, while the married woman cares for how to please her husband (1 Corinthians 7:34).

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 7:35, Paul mentions he speaks for what purpose?
options: To cast a snare upon you
questions.explanation: Paul clarifies that his guidance is for the benefit and profit of the believers, not to impose burdens on them (1 Corinthians 7:35).

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 7:39, when is a wife at liberty to marry?
questions.explanation: Paul states that a wife is bound by law as long as her husband lives, but if he dies, she is free to marry whom she wishes, only in the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:39).

questions.question: What does Paul imply about the time in 1 Corinthians 7:29?
questions.explanation: Paul emphasizes the brevity of time, urging believers to live with urgency and spiritual awareness (1 Corinthians 7:29).

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Corinthians 7:36, Paul states that a man sins if he marries his virgin.
questions.explanation: Paul indicates that a man does not sin if he marries his virgin if the circumstances require it (1 Corinthians 7:36).

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 7:38, what is said about giving a virgin in marriage?
options: It is better not to marry
questions.explanation: Paul states that the one who gives her in marriage does well, but he who does not gives her not in marriage does better (1 Corinthians 7:38).

questions.question: What does Paul mean by 'the fashion of this world passeth away' in 1 Corinthians 7:31?
questions.explanation: Paul points out that the transient nature of worldly matters should guide believers to prioritize spiritual matters (1 Corinthians 7:31).

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Corinthians 7:40, Paul believes a widow would be happier if she remarries.
questions.explanation: Paul states that a widow would be happier if she remains as she is, according to his judgment (1 Corinthians 7:40).

questions.question: Which Old Testament theme is echoed in 1 Corinthians 7:14 regarding the sanctification of the family?
options: The concept of clean and unclean
questions.correctAnswer: The concept of clean and unclean
questions.explanation: Paul states that an unbelieving spouse is sanctified by the believing spouse, reminiscent of Old Testament purity laws concerning clean and unclean (1 Corinthians 7:14).

questions.question: In the context of 1 Corinthians 7:32-33, how does Paul differentiate the concerns of a married man from an unmarried man?
options: Married men focus on worldly things
Married men are free from care
questions.correctAnswer: Married men focus on worldly things
questions.explanation: Paul explains that a married man cares for the things of the world, how he may please his wife, contrasting with the unmarried man's focus on pleasing the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:32-33).

questions.question: What Greek word meaning 'to please' is significant in 1 Corinthians 7:32-33 regarding marital responsibilities?
questions.explanation: The Greek term 'Aresko' translates to 'to please', highlighting the responsibilities of marital relationships in this chapter (1 Corinthians 7:32-33).

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:1 indicate about touching a woman?
options: It is good for a man not to touch a woman
It is sinful to touch a woman
It is better to touch a woman than to marry
questions.correctAnswer: It is good for a man not to touch a woman
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:1 clearly states that 'It is good for a man not to touch a woman', indicating a principle of sexual restraint for those not married.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 7:4, who has power over the body in a marriage?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:4 states that 'the wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife', emphasizing mutual authority in marriage.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:9 suggest about marriage and self-control?
options: It is better to be single than to marry
It is better to marry than to burn
questions.correctAnswer: It is better to marry than to burn
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:9 states, 'if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn', suggesting that marriage is a legitimate solution for those struggling with self-control.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 7:14, how are children described in relation to an unbelieving spouse?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:14 indicates that 'the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife' and 'your children...are holy', suggesting that the faith of one spouse has a sanctifying effect on the family.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:20 advise about one's calling?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:20 instructs, 'Let every man abide in the same calling wherein he was called', emphasizing the importance of remaining steadfast in one's current situation.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 10-11 convey regarding marriage?
options: Divorce is allowed for any reason
Wives should not depart from their husbands
Husbands can put away their wives at will
questions.correctAnswer: Wives should not depart from their husbands
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 command that 'Let not the wife depart from her husband' and if she does, she should remain unmarried or reconcile, stressing the permanence of marriage.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:35 indicate about distractions in service to the Lord?
options: Service to the Lord should be without distraction
questions.correctAnswer: Service to the Lord should be without distraction
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:35 states, 'I speak for your own profit...that ye may attend upon the Lord without distraction', highlighting the need for focus in spiritual matters.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 7:27, what should a person do if they are bound to a wife?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:27 advises, 'Art thou bound unto a wife? seek not to be loosed', reinforcing the commitment within marriage.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:38 imply about marriage decisions?
options: Those who marry do well, but those who do not marry do better
questions.correctAnswer: Those who marry do well, but those who do not marry do better
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:38 states, 'he that giveth her in marriage doeth well; but he that giveth her not in marriage doeth better', suggesting a preference for remaining single under certain circumstances.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Ye are bought with a price' in 1 Corinthians 7:23 teach about believers?
options: They are free from all obligations
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:23 states, 'Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men', indicating that believers are owned by God due to Christ's sacrifice.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:15 imply about departing from an unbelieving spouse?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:15 clarifies, 'if the unbelieving depart, let him depart...but God hath called us to peace', permitting separation in certain circumstances.

questions.question: What attribute of God is reflected in 1 Corinthians 7:6 regarding commands?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:6 states, 'But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment', reflecting God's mercy in allowing choice rather than imposing strict commands.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 7:32-33 describe the focus of unmarried versus married individuals?
options: Both are equally focused on the Lord
Married individuals focus on worldly things
Unmarried individuals focus only on family
questions.correctAnswer: Married individuals focus on worldly things
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:32-33 contrasts the unmarried, who 'careth for the things that belong to the Lord', with married individuals, who 'careth for the things that are of the world', highlighting differing priorities.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 7:18 teach about circumcision and calling?
options: One should change their circumcision status
One should remain in their calling
questions.correctAnswer: One should remain in their calling
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:18 instructs, 'let him not become uncircumcised...let him not be circumcised', emphasizing the importance of remaining in the calling received from God.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Bible endorses marriage as a societal norm without exception. What does 1 Corinthians 7:28 actually teach?
options: Marrying is not a sin, but may lead to trouble
Marriage is the only option for believers
questions.correctAnswer: Marrying is not a sin, but may lead to trouble
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:28 states, 'if thou marry, thou hast not sinned...Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh: but I spare you', indicating that while marriage is not sinful, it does carry challenges.
